regions.name: flow_far_wake
regions.why: The far-wake requirement volume is also uncovered (coverage 0.0). Level 2 gives h = 0.375/2^2 = 0.09375 m, under the required 0.175 m span cap, and is deliberately one level coarser than the near wake to bound cost of the slowly recovering deficit, matching the stated mechanism that far-wake transport is coarsenable. It is the same size as the existing 0.28125 m distance shell, so the wake box merges without a stair-step.

regions.name: flow_aft_shear_core
regions.why: Mechanism, not score-chasing: the dimensionless estimate discharges an aft-body boundary layer of about 0.0489 m, which is only ~1.04 level-3 cells (0.046875 m), so the emerging shear layer and velocity-deficit edge behind the trailing edge would be smeared over a single cell. Level 4 halves the cell to 0.0234375 m (~2 cells across the estimated discharge thickness) in the first 1.0 m of wake, where the cross-stream gradient is steepest, while leaving the rest of the near wake at level 3 and the far wake at 2. Lateral extent is kept identical to the near-wake box so the shear layer is not clipped by a lateral refinement boundary; the only level change is a single 4->3 step in streamwise direction, within n_cells_between_levels = 3. Level 4 is within +2 of the global surface level 3. This is a hypothesis-driven resolution increase expected to matter only for the near-field deficit; it is not evidence that the wake is accurately resolved.

regions.name: repair_0
regions.why: actual layer deficit concentrated in measured boundary faces

regions.name: flow_near_wake
regions.why: No-regression guard on the near-wake requirement only: flow_requirement:near_wake needs native p95 axis span <= 0.0875 m and the measured anchor delivered 0.0472 m at level 3 (0.375/2^3 = 0.046875 m), so level 3 is re-asserted to keep the corridor certified after the restore. Bounds match the requirement exactly, so no new level jump is introduced. The far wake is deliberately NOT refined: flow_requirement:far_wake measured 0.0943 m against its 0.175 m cap (1.86x margin) at level 2, and spending 8x cells per refinement increment there would only take budget away from the layer repair this attempt needs.

advisor.hypothesis: Restore the best measured anchor (plan:605313bf946a3459, coverage 0.8983, fidelity accepted, native quality n_failed=0) and fix the residual LOCAL cap-band defect by the mechanism actually named in the native layer log: the displacementMedialAxis mover is dropping columns at points where thickness-to-medial distance is large and where isolated non-extruded points spread. layer_shortfall:0 shows the deficit is NOT space-limited (solid_normal_half_thickness p50 0.325 m, p5 0.212 m vs a requested stack of 0.0160 m, >13x margin; dihedral p95 5.53 deg; fraction of adjacent edges above layer feature_angle 0.0), and the native thickness-truncation diagnostic retained 0 lines — so the mover is stopping columns, not thinning them. The lever is medial-distance awareness and column contiguity: cap the extrusion height against medial distance more conservatively (max_thickness_to_medial_ratio 0.3 -> 0.15) so surviving columns stay well inside the fluid medial limit, relax min_medial_axis_angle 90 -> 60 (a blunt spheroid cap presents fluid medial directions across the full angle range; 90 over-restricts and zeros columns), add one conservative n_grow=1 so neighbouring points are stopped TOGETHER at the cap band instead of each face independently, and give the mover/snapper more iterations so the extrusion-direction field converges across the cap. feature_angle returns to 60 (measured: 150 gave 0.8581 vs 0.8983 at 60) and the anchor's exact first_height 0.001237896307075701 is retained, preserving estimated y+ p50 = 50.0. Unknown: whether the residual 11.7% band is a medial-cap regime or a snap normal defect; the two actions below test the medial-contiguity hypothesis first because the native log names it, while the snap improvement is a no-regression input-quality change. This is not asserted as a physical certificate.
advisor.expected_change: Measurable: body area fraction with >=5 actual layers rises from the anchor's 0.8983 to >=0.90 (gate), with the 0-4 layer residue on the cap bands (currently 0.9449 at 4 layers, 0.0188 at 0 across the measured region) reduced; native quality stays accepted (max_non_ortho <= 65 gate; anchor 57.6) and fidelity stays accepted (bidirectional p99 << 0.015 m). Cell count expected 3.0e5-3.6e5, well under the 2e6 budget. Near-wake native p95 span must stay <= 0.0875 m (measured 0.0472 m) and far-wake <= 0.175 m (measured 0.0943 m) — the anchor's wake regions are restored unchanged. Uncertainty: if the blocked faces are a snap/normal-coherence rather than medial-distance problem, coverage may stay near 0.898 and the next intervention must move to the snap/normal path; no flow-accuracy or y+ validation is claimed, and actual first height remains unmeasured.
alternatives: Author a brand-new full spec from the current round1 configuration without restoring; rejected because the anchor's measured 0.8983 beats every other measured candidate (0.0033, 0.0, 0.8581), and restore-first is required.

Increase resolution (local_refine/surface_level, or re-asserting the level-4 repair_0 box) to fill the missing layers; rejected as evidence-contradicted — round0/9ed11ed69256a0de already ran level-4 repair_0 plus stronger normal smoothing and still reached only 0.8581, and the stack fits by >13x, so resolution is not the lever.

Re-enable the motion-solver shrinker (displacementMotionSolver); not chosen this round — the torus counterexample leaves 1.74% coverage from shrinker change alone and the anchor's medial mover already passes quality (max_non_ortho 57.6 vs 65), so it is reserved as the next distinct mechanism if the medial-contiguity change fails.

Raise n_surface_layers to 8 (round0's value) for stack margin; not chosen because the measured deficit is 0-4 layers, and the anchor's 7 already reached 86.7% of area at exactly 7 while the requested stack 0.0160 m is 13x inside the available 0.212 m, so extra layers add iteration risk without addressing column suppression.

Use wall_height to rescale first height; inadmissible — no numerically sane measured flow field exists (flow_probe_sanity null, actual_yplus unavailable), so wall-shear-based calibration cannot be cited.
counterevidence: round0 plan:9ed11ed69256a0de (feature_angle 150, n_grow 0, min_medial_axis_angle 60, strong normal smoothing) reached only 0.8581 < anchor 0.8983, so angle relaxation plus smoothing alone is not sufficient — this plan keeps feature_angle at the measured-better 60 and adds the medial-ratio cap and grow coupling.
